content.title: About
content.content: Raw ground lamb is made from lean cuts of lamb that are finely minced into a pink, soft paste. It has a distinctive mild gamey flavor and a tender texture. Ground lamb is used in a variety of dishes such as burgers, kebabs, stews, and meat sauces.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Lamb is generally more tender than beef because its muscle fibers are finer.
In many Mediterranean countries, ground lamb is a staple for dishes like kofta and moussaka.
Raw ground lamb cooks quickly, making it ideal for stir‑fries and quick sautés.
Lamb provides heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.
In traditional Middle Eastern cuisine, lamb is a symbol of celebration and hospitality.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Lamb supplies complete protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Rich in vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 supports nerve function and the formation of red blood cells.

items.title: Contains zinc
items.content: Zinc is important for immune health and wound healing.

items.title: Good source of iron
items.content: Heme iron from lamb helps prevent iron‑deficiency anemia.

items.title: Provides selenium
items.content: Selenium acts as an antioxidant and supports thyroid function.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Raw ground lamb can harbor pathogens such as E. coli and Salmonella; cook to an internal temperature of at least 71 °C.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to lamb.

items.title: High in saturated fat
items.content: Excessive consumption may contribute to elevated cholesterol levels.

items.title: Purine content
items.content: People with gout should limit intake of lamb.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Ground lamb should be cooked before eating: pan‑fry, grill, bake, or simmer. It works well in burgers, meatballs, kebabs, stuffed vegetables, and classic dishes like shepherd’s pie or lamb ragù.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep ground lamb refrigerated at 0‑4 °C and use within 2 days. For longer storage, freeze in an airtight bag at ‑18 °C, where it remains good for 3‑4 months. Discard if it develops a sour or off odor.
